_readme: kleinerperkins.com WordPress REST (/wp-json/wp/v2/person, 30 published people; role from the person_role taxonomy), pulled 2026-09-30 by scratch/pull-wp.py, flattened by scratch/shape-site.py.

rows.name: Leo Shao
rows.title: Investor
rows.bio: Leo joined Kleiner Perkins in 2026 and focuses on growth-stage investments. Prior to Kleiner Perkins, Leo was investing at private equity firm TPG Capital and started his career at Morgan Stanley where he helped advise on multi-billion-dollar M&A transactions and financings. Leo grew up in New Jersey and graduated from Harvard with a BA in Applied Mathematics and Computer Science. Outside of work, Leo loves trying new restaurants and spending time outdoors playing tennis, golf, and skiing.

rows.name: Aatish Nayak
rows.title: Partner
rows.bio: Aatish joined Kleiner Perkins as a partner in May 2026 where he focuses on partnering with AI native founders with deep vertical expertise across all domains. Prior to joining Kleiner Perkins, Aatish was the first PM and VP of Product at Harvey, where he helped build the early product, design, marketing, analytics, and support teams. Before that he was an early product leader at Scale AI working on data infrastructure for ecommerce, early NLP (GPT-2), and autonomous vehicles. rows.name: Camille Manso
rows.title: Business Development
rows.bio: Camille Manso joined Kleiner Perkins in 2026 to build and activate partnerships between the firm’s venture ecosystem and leading global corporations. She works with founders and enterprise leaders as a connector and strategic advisor, helping them identify and execute high-impact collaborations that accelerate AI adoption, unlock new enterprise markets, and drive commercial growth. Prior to Kleiner Perkins, Camille was a Partner at Silicon Foundry, where she spent five years advising F500 executives on innovation strategy and emerging technologies, architecting platforms that bridge corporates

rows.name: Ted Schlein
rows.title: Partner and Advisor
rows.bio: Ted Schlein is a partner at Kleiner Perkins, and executive chairman and founding partner at Ballistic Ventures. He has spent the last 35 years helping create transformative companies. A Midas of investing and the former chairman of the National Venture Capital Association (NVCA), Ted has funded, supported, and guided more than 30 founders to successful company exits including ArcSight, Chegg, Fortify Software, IronNet Cybersecurity, Jive, LifeLock and Segment. He currently serves on the boards of Apiiro, Bedrock, Chegg (CHGG), FullStory, Interos, Incorta, IronNet, Rebellion Defense, Reputation

rows.name: Ryan Panchadsaram
rows.title: Advisor to the Chairman
rows.bio: Ryan Panchadsaram joined Kleiner Perkins in 2016 to focus on venture-stage companies across the firm and serve as technical advisor to John Doerr, Chair of Kleiner Perkins. Ryan was the Deputy Chief Technology Officer for the United States. At the White House, Ryan helped shape how an $80 billion budget can be used by federal agencies to deliver on their missions in a more effective, design-centric, and data-driven way. rows.name: Wen Hsieh
rows.title: Advisor
rows.bio: Wen Hsieh is an advisor at Kleiner Perkins where he focuses on supporting hardware-related investments. Before joining Kleiner Perkins, Wen was an associate principal at McKinsey & Company San Francisco and a leader of McKinsey’s Asia semiconductor practice. During his five years at McKinsey, he focused primarily on serving leading companies across the global semiconductor value chain. Wen’s secondary focus at McKinsey was on the North America biopharma sector. Earlier in his career, he founded OnChip Technologies, a startup developing MEMS microfluidic biochips. rows.name: Bing Gordon
rows.title: Advisor
rows.bio: Bing Gordon joined Kleiner Perkins in 2008 and serves as Chief Product Officer and advisor for the firm. Bing also leads Kleiner Perkins’ sFund, the investment initiative to fund and build applications and services that deliver on the promise of the social web. The sFund, launched in 2010 with strategic partners Amazon.com, Facebook, Zynga, Comcast, Liberty Media and Allen & Co., has made 16 investments to date, including four seeds. Bing serves on the board of directors of Amazon, N3twork, Zazzle and Zynga. He was also a founding director at Katango (acquired by Google 2011), ngmoco (acquired

rows.name: Al Gore
rows.title: Advisor
rows.bio: Former Vice President Al Gore is the cofounder and chairman of Generation Investment Management, and the founder and chairman of The Climate Reality Project, a nonprofit devoted to solving the climate crisis. He is also a senior partner at Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers and a member of Apple Inc.’s board of directors. Gore was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 1976, 1978, 1980, and 1982 and to the U.S. Senate in 1984 and 1990. He was inaugurated as the 45th vice president of the United States on January 20, 1993, and served eight years. He is the author of the #1 New York Times

rows.name: John Doerr
rows.title: Chairman
rows.bio: John is an engineer, venture capitalist, and the chair of Kleiner Perkins. He is the author of bestsellers Measure What Matters and Speed and Scale: An Action Plan for Solving Our Climate Crisis Now. For over 40 years, John has served entrepreneurs with ingenuity and optimism, helping them build bold teams and disruptive companies. A pioneer of Silicon Valley’s cleantech movement, he has invested in zero-emissions technologies since 2006. Outside Kleiner Perkins, John works with social entrepreneurs who are tackling systemic issues across climate, public health, and education.

rows.name: Brook Byers
rows.title: Founder
rows.bio: Brook Byers has been a venture capital investor since 1972. He has been closely involved with founders to help build more than 60 new technology-based companies. He formed the first life sciences practice group in the venture capital profession in 1984 and led Kleiner Perkins to become a premier venture capital firm in the life sciences, healthcare and biotechnology sectors. Brook was the founding president and then chairman of four biotechnology companies that were incubated in Kleiner Perkins’ offices and went on to become public companies with an aggregate market value of more than US$8 bil

rows.name: Lauren Schultz
rows.title: Operating Partner, Business Development
rows.bio: Lauren Schultz joined Kleiner Perkins in 2022 to build the business development function and now serves as the link between our venture capital ecosystem and the corporate world. Lauren creates opportunities to accelerate AI transformation and digital innovation through market research, peer-to-peer connections, industry thought leadership, and work with our portfolio companies. Prior to Kleiner Perkins, Lauren spent six years as an Enterprise Account Executive at Amazon Web Services and five years as a Commercial Account Executive at EMC (now Dell Technologies).

rows.name: Dana Schafer-Smith
rows.title: Technical Talent
rows.bio: Dana leads Technical Talent for Kleiner Perkins. She supports the firm’s portfolio companies by connecting them with exceptional engineers and builders, and oversees the Kleiner Perkins Fellows Program. Previously, Dana supported the engineering organizations at Pinterest and Grammarly through early talent, technical recruiting, and recruiting operations. Her career has been shaped by a deep focus on identifying high-potential talent and designing programs that accelerate growth. rows.name: Athena Ruland
rows.title: Experience Marketing
rows.bio: Athena Ruland joined Kleiner Perkins in 2019 where she leads experience marketing, bringing the brand to life for the firm, and supports its portfolio. Athena was instrumental in starting the Grit podcast, and was responsible for its production for the first 230 episodes. Prior to Kleiner Perkins, Athena was part of the VMG Partners team. She previously worked on the equity sales teams at J.P. Morgan and Deutsche Bank. Athena began her career at the County of San Mateo as an analyst. Outside of work, Athena enjoys traveling, spending time with her family and volunteering for Muttville, an orga

rows.name: Joubin Mirzadegan
rows.title: Partner
rows.bio: Joubin is a Partner at Kleiner Perkins, where he leads the portfolio operating team, and CEO and co-founder of Roadrunner, the firm's first incubation since Glean. Joubin joined Kleiner Perkins in 2019 where he has helped founders and their teams build and scale go-to-market organizations. He advises KP portfolio companies on all aspects of building and scaling a robust go-to-market, and enables the firm's portfolio through high-impact relationships with executives and key ecosystem partners. Prior to Kleiner Perkins, Joubin built and led multiple sales organizations through successful acquisi

rows.name: Jesse King
rows.title: Partner, General Counsel
rows.bio: Jesse is the General Counsel of Kleiner Perkins. He oversees all legal matters in connection with the firm and its portfolio companies. Prior to joining the firm in 2019, Jesse was an attorney at Fenwick & West, where his practice focused on venture capital, M&A, and general corporate, and securities matters. Prior to joining Fenwick, Jesse served as a law clerk to the Honorable Steven V. Wilson and was an associate at Munger, Tolles & Olson. Before attending law school, he worked in the business process and compliance group at Google. Jesse holds a JD from Harvard Law School and a BA from the

rows.name: Lindsey Keller
rows.title: Go to Market Talent
rows.bio: Lindsey leads talent for Kleiner Perkins, supporting 200+ portfolio companies with GTM + G&A recruiting, talent strategy, and community building. She partners with early-stage founders as both a fractional recruiter and talent advisor - building founding teams, filling mission-critical leadership roles, and providing strategic guidance on org design, compensation benchmarking, and interview frameworks. Previously, Lindsey was an early team member at Artisanal Talent, a boutique executive search firm, where she rose from Associate to Partner and placed 100+ GTM leaders at venture-backed B2B Saa

rows.name: Suzanne Holloway
rows.title: Operating Partner, Marketing
rows.bio: Suzanne is a Go-to-Market Operating Partner focused on marketing. She works with Kleiner Perkins portfolio companies as a GTM advisor and a hands-on fractional marketing leader. She helps founders define marketing strategy and build high-performing teams by recruiting talent and establishing operating rhythms. Before joining Kleiner Perkins in 2022, Suzanne built marketing from scratch to scale at several startups. Most recently, she was one of the first go-to-market hires at Miro, where she led global demand generation and enterprise marketing during the company's climb to a $17.5 billion val

rows.name: Moustafa ElBialy
rows.title: Chief Information Officer
rows.bio: Moustafa (Mous) joined Kleiner Perkins in 2018 as Chief Information Officer. With over 30 years of technology experience, including more than two decades dedicated to venture capital, Moustafa oversees the firm’s technology strategy, AI initiatives, infrastructure, cybersecurity, data, and business intelligence operations. A veteran of the industry, Moustafa has scaled technology operations from the ground up at three of Silicon Valley's leading venture capital firms. Prior to Kleiner Perkins, he served as Director of Technology at Social Capital and previously spent over eight years at Sequoi

rows.name: Candy Cheng
rows.title: Head of Marketing & Communications
rows.bio: Candy Cheng is a producer, storyteller, and content creator. She joined Kleiner Perkins in 2025 after leading content at Initialized Capital. Before venture, Candy built a career in journalism, most recently as a senior correspondent at Business Insider covering startups and VC. She previously produced conversations with leaders like Tim Cook, Bill Gates, and Jack Ma as an executive producer at Bloomberg Television and worked on CNBC’s Mad Money w/ Jim Cramer. Candy holds a bachelor’s in International Relations from USC and a master’s in Journalism from Columbia. Outside of work, she’s a ceram

rows.name: Susan Biglieri
rows.title: Chief Financial Officer & Chief Operating Officer
rows.bio: Susan (Sue) Biglieri is the CFO and COO at Kleiner Perkins. With over 30 years of experience at the firm, she is responsible for the financial and operational functions. Sue is an active member of the NVCA CFO Task Force and the VC COO Collective. Prior to Kleiner Perkins, she was the controller at startup Mouse Systems Technology. Sue began her career at Ernst & Young after graduating from University of California at Berkeley with a bachelor’s degree in business administration. She is a CPA (retired) in the state of California.

rows.name: Tomas Barreto
rows.title: Operating Partner, Engineering
rows.bio: As the engineering operating partner, Tomas advises portfolio companies on building and scaling their engineering organizations. As the fifth engineer and fourteenth employee at Box, Tomas spent over nine years scaling the engineering team through IPO and $500M+ in revenue. As VP of engineering, he led teams of 150+ and built the technical foundation for Box’s long-term success. Tomas later joined Checkr as the first VP of engineering, scaling the engineering, product, and design team from 25 to more than 100 people. Tomas then co-founded Okay, an engineering effectiveness startup used by comp

rows.name: Lucas Oliveira
rows.title: Principal
rows.bio: Lucas joined Kleiner Perkins in 2023 and focuses on investments in enterprise software and cybersecurity. Prior to joining Kleiner Perkins, he worked on several multi-billion dollar take-private transactions at software private equity fund Thoma Bravo. Lucas began his career at Morgan Stanley, advising on acquisitions and financings. He moved from Brazil to Colorado when he was young and graduated from the University of Colorado Boulder. Outside of work, he loves to stay active, whether skiing, running, or playing soccer.

rows.name: Aditya Naganath
rows.title: Partner
rows.bio: Aditya Naganath is a Partner at Kleiner Perkins with a focus on artificial intelligence, enterprise software applications, infrastructure and security. He has made investments in companies such as Sail, Traversal, Wisdom, and Maxima, and serves on the boards of several as either a director or observer. Prior to joining Kleiner Perkins, Aditya was a product manager at Google focusing on growth initiatives for the next billion users team. He previously was a technical lead at Palantir Technologies and formerly held software engineering roles at Twitter and Nextdoor, where he was a Kleiner Perkin

rows.name: Ilya Fushman
rows.title: Partner
rows.bio: Ilya Fushman is a Partner at Kleiner Perkins. He invests in early and growth stage companies that aim to fundamentally reshape industries through technology and novel business models. He has invested in and sits on the boards of companies including Harvey, Rippling, Profound, NewLimit, Saronic, Motive, Stord, Chai Discovery, Mind Robotics and has previously backed companies such as Slack, Loom and Intercom. rows.name: Josh Coyne
rows.title: Partner
rows.bio: Josh Coyne is a Partner at Kleiner Perkins, where he invests in startups applying AI across software and hardware. He has invested in companies including Armadin, Browserbase, CuspAI, Garner Health, OpenEvidence, Stord, Synthesia, and TerraFirma. Prior to joining Kleiner Perkins in 2017, Josh was at Qatalyst Partners, where he advised on multi-billion-dollar acquisitions, leveraged buyouts, and financings across a variety of technology sectors. rows.name: Nadia Cochinwala
rows.title: Principal
rows.bio: Nadia joined Kleiner Perkins in 2023 and focuses on investments in enterprise applications and infrastructure. Prior to Kleiner Perkins, Nadia was investing at TPG and Bridgewater Associates and started her career at Evercore where she advised across multi billion dollar acquisitions and financings across a variety of technology sectors. Nadia was born and raised in the Bay Area and graduated from UC Berkeley, where she competed on the Parliamentary Debate team. Outside of work, Nadia loves trying new workout classes, exploring coffee shops, and hunting for the Bay’s best libraries/bookstores.

rows.name: Annie Case
rows.title: Advisor
rows.bio: Annie Case is an Advisor to Kleiner Perkins, where she previously served as a Partner focused on investments across consumer technology, digital health, and enterprise software. She continues to work closely with the teams at Phia, Subject, Lotus Health, and Health Universe. Prior to Kleiner Perkins, Annie worked in product and business operations at Uber, where she supported the SVP of operations and helped scale the Uber Eats business to new markets internationally. rows.name: Leigh Marie Braswell
rows.title: Partner
rows.bio: Leigh Marie Braswell is a Partner at Kleiner Perkins, where she backs founders building the next generation of infrastructure and AI applications. She has invested in and sits on the boards of Avoca and Poetic, and has also backed companies including Nooks, Applied Compute, and Engram. Her notable past investments include Windsurf, Neon, and Chronosphere. Prior to joining Kleiner Perkins in 2023, Leigh Marie began her investing career at Founders Fund. rows.name: Mamoon Hamid
rows.title: Partner
rows.bio: Mamoon Hamid is a Partner at Kleiner Perkins, where he backs founders building the next generation of transformative technology companies. Over the past two decades, he has been an investor in many category-defining companies including Anthropic, Applied Intuition, Box, Figma, Glean, Granola, Intercom, Netskope, Moveworks, OpenEvidence, Parallel, Rippling, Rogo, Slack, Together AI and Waymo. He began his career as an engineer at Xilinx, a Kleiner Perkins-backed company, before moving into venture capital in 2005 at USVP, where he became a Partner.
